cases.sentence: На зарево первого занявшегося 2-го сентября пожара, с ___ и с разными чувствами смотрели убегавшие и уезжавшие жители и отступавшие войска.
cases.explain: «разных дорог» — after the preposition «с», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: The glow of the first fire that began on the second of September was watched from the various roads by the fugitive Muscovites and by the retreating troops, with many different feelings.

cases.sentence: На зарево первого занявшегося 2-го сентября пожара, с разных дорог и с ___ смотрели убегавшие и уезжавшие жители и отступавшие войска.
cases.explain: «разными чувствами» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: The glow of the first fire that began on the second of September was watched from the various roads by the fugitive Muscovites and by the retreating troops, with many different feelings.

cases.sentence: В 10 часов, господа Ростовы и раненые, ехавшие с ними, все разместились по дворам и избам ___.
cases.explain: «большого села» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: The Rostóv party spent the night at Mytíshchi, fourteen miles from Moscow. They had started so late on the first of September, the road had been so blocked by vehicles and troops, so many things had been forgotten for which servants were sent back, that they had decided to spend that night at a place three miles out of Moscow. The next morning they woke late and were again delayed so often that they only got as far as Great Mytíshchi. At ten o’clock that evening the Rostóv family and the wounded traveling with them were all distributed in the yards and huts of that large village. The Rostóvs’ servants and coachmen and the orderlies of the wounded officers, after attending to their masters, had supper, fed the horses, and came out into the porches.

cases.sentence: В соседней избе лежал ___ Раевского, с разбитою кистью руки, и страшная боль, которую он чувствовал, заставляла его жалобно не переставая стонать, и стоны эти страшно звучали в осенней темноте ночи.
cases.explain: «раненый адъютант» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: In a neighboring hut lay Raévski’s adjutant with a fractured wrist. The awful pain he suffered made him moan incessantly and piteously, and his moaning sounded terrible in the darkness of the autumn night. He had spent the first night in the same yard as the Rostóvs. The countess said she had been unable to close her eyes on account of his moaning, and at Mytíshchi she moved into a worse hut simply to be farther away from the wounded man.

cases.sentence: Один из людей в темноте ночи, из-за ___ стоявшей у подъезда кареты, заметил другое небольшое зарево пожара.
cases.explain: «высокого кузова» — after the preposition «из-за», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: In the darkness of the night one of the servants noticed, above the high body of a coach standing before the porch, the small glow of another fire. One glow had long been visible and everybody knew that it was Little Mytíshchi burning—set on fire by Mamónov’s Cossacks.

cases.sentence: Одно зарево давно уже видно было, и все знали, что это горели Малые Мытищи, зажженные ___.
cases.explain: «Мамоновскими казаками» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: In the darkness of the night one of the servants noticed, above the high body of a coach standing before the porch, the small glow of another fire. One glow had long been visible and everybody knew that it was Little Mytíshchi burning—set on fire by Mamónov’s Cossacks.

cases.sentence: — А ведь это, братцы, ___, — сказал денщик.
cases.explain: «другой пожар» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “But look here, brothers, there’s another fire!” remarked an orderly. All turned their attention to the glow.

cases.sentence: Послышались вздохи, слова молитвы и всхлипывание старого ___.
cases.explain: «графского камердинера» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Who’s to put it out?” Danílo Teréntich, who had hitherto been silent, was heard to say. His voice was calm and deliberate. “Moscow it is, brothers,” said he. “Mother Moscow, the white …” his voice faltered, and he gave way to an old man’s sob. And it was as if they had all only waited for this to realize the significance for them of the glow they were watching. Sighs were heard, words of prayer, and the sobbing of the count’s old valet.
